key_insight: A Gaussian-process state-space model learns latent material memory directly from stress–strain histories, replacing prescribed constitutive forms and internal variables.
engineering_relevance: Integration into Abaqus/Explicit enables finite-element simulation of history-dependent, pressure-sensitive quasi-brittle materials with GP-based uncertainty estimates.
method: Evolve latent history states using current stress invariants and equivalent-strain increments.
Map latent states and current strain to six-component stress using a sparse multi-output GP trained by variational inference.
Export the learned constitutive update through an Abaqus/Explicit user material subroutine.
evidence_signal: Four verification cases assess held-out history rollouts, changing confinement, frozen-memory unloading–reloading, and multi-element structural response consistent with KCC.
watch_item: The reported checks do not establish reliability beyond the evaluated loading paths; unloading–reloading uses a frozen-memory extension.
paper_title: A Gaussian Process State Space Formulation for Materials Constitutive Modeling: Application to Quasi-brittle Materials
